title: Military news for Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck, 1744, in a three-digit code (HStAM 118 a Nr. 3954, ff. 3-4; HCPortal 517)

documents.shelfmark: Hessisches Staatsarchiv Marburg, HStAM 118 a Nr. 3954, ff. 3r-4r; HCPortal record 517
documents.date: 1744 (probably the correspondent's letter of 18 January 1744 answered in the draft on f. 4v)
documents.route: unknown correspondent -> Prince Carl August Friedrich of Waldeck-Pyrmont
documents.language: German (probably: salutation and the two clear-text addresses are German)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaves, in the file (8 images on Arcinsys) or in print. f. 4v carries the prince's French draft reply in clear, which gives context only.

transcription.source: Read from the HCPortal/Arcinsys scans (2908 x 3214 and 2618 x 3044 px) in full-resolution line crops; trans_p1.txt, trans_p2.txt.
transcription.notes: Two writer's corrections resolved (f. 4 l. 5 struck 9x -> 7; l. 13 struck 97 -> 8); a few doubtful digits marked ?. f. 4 writes 2 as a z-shaped figure.

system.summary: Probably a two-part homophonic nomenclator of about a thousand numbers (letters with a few scattered numbers, syllables and words with one), numbered without alphabetical order; codes under 100 used most.
system.sibling_key: none found: no key, decipherment or other letter in this code in HStAM 118 a (Arcinsys), HCPortal or DECODE; the Hessen-Kassel keys checked (4 d Nr. 1229, 1231, 1237) do not fit
system.notes: Dot-separated groups 4-999; 717 tokens, 303 distinct, 144 used once, no immediate repeats. 879.144.X.126 recurs four times with X = 90, 7, 7, 924 and the writer struck a 9 and wrote 7 in one: homophones. Token mass along the numbers matches no alphabetical, column or multiplicative order; the profile matches a synthetic two-part nomenclator (310 types, 146 singletons).

prior_solution.where: HCPortal: not solved. Nothing in print or on DECODE found.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the target with /goal from the hand-scored candidate list (research/oldest/scan_2026-09-23). No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: C# (csc 4.0): homophonic, monotone and heat-bath annealers

solution.what: HCPortal images of ff. 3r-4r (media 1448, 1449); all 8 Arcinsys images of the file: wrapper, f. 3v docket 'Schreiben an [blank] in Ziffern', f. 4v French draft reply.

Arcinsys searches across all Hessian archives for cipher items (Chiffre, chiffriert, dechiffriert, Ziffern, Geheimschrift...); HCPortal records 494-523 and all 319 keys; BLKÖ biography of the prince. No key, decipherment or sibling letter; the 1744 volumes (118 a Nr. 1973-1980) are undigitised.
45 lines transcribed from full-resolution crops (trans_p1.txt, trans_p2.txt): 717 groups, 303 distinct; two writer's corrections resolved.
The French draft on f. 4v read: the prince answers a letter of 18 January (New Year wishes, news) and promises a vacancy in his regiment; the cipher letter is most probably that letter.

Frequencies, repeats, shared contexts: flat profile (top group 2%), 879.144.X.126 x4 with X = 90/7/7/924 and a struck 9 corrected to 7 (homophones), no immediate repeats, codes under 100 used twice as often.

Letter-level homophonic synthetic of the same size and profile: a 5-gram annealer finds gibberish scoring as well as or better than the true plaintext (modern model -1234 vs -1408; 1740s model -1090.5 vs -1094.4).

Word-segmentation term (unigram 1740s word model, Viterbi) added: the true key now scores highest on the control (-2173) but annealing (12 x 20 M moves, -2340) and heat-bath sampling (-2679) do not reach it.
Letter-level annealer with the 1740s 5-gram on the real text: best -1107.5, restarts disagree, no German.
One-part (alphabetical) code: token-mass KS test against German syllabary usage rejects natural order over 1-999 (0.192 vs random 0.077) and over 100-999 (0.149).

Hessen-Kassel keys in Marburg (HCPortal; DECODE's 112 records of 1710-1799) listed; 4 d Nr. 1220 f. 12 and Nr. 1231 show column-numbered alphabetical syllabaries; Nr. 1231, 1229 (R4680) and 1237 (R4741, R4742) do not fit this letter.
Column-numbered one-part code as in the Hessian keys (units digit = column), cyclic orders and multiplicative numberings: no better fit than random numberings.

Monotone annealers (after swieten1757/msolve.py) with free codes under 100, per-digit chains, Hessian remap, heat-bath sampling: stall below the truth on alphabetical controls; fragment soup on the real text.

Two-part nomenclator synthetic after R4680 (letters with 4 homophones, 600 syllables and words) reproduces the real profile (310 types, 146 singletons, top 14); on it the true key scores -1934 / -1284 while blind runs find gibberish at -1060 / -255: the key is not identifiable from 717 groups.
New Year wish implied by the reply ('zu dem angetretenen neuen Jahre', fitting the line-1 hyphen if groups were letters): cannot be placed in a two-part code with unknown unit boundaries.

outcome.method_basis: No key exists online; the system was characterised as a two-part homophonic nomenclator and synthetic controls of the same design and size show that 717 groups do not identify such a key, so ciphertext-only solving was closed.
outcome.fraction_read_source: ct.txt: 0 of 717 cipher tokens given a value

gaps.detail: two-part nomenclator, no key on Arcinsys, HCPortal or DECODE; one letter is too little to rebuild it (synthetic control)

gaps.item: further traffic or a deciphered copy in HStAM 118 a Nr. 1973 (Feldzug 1744 Bd. 1) and Nr. 1969-1972, 2044, 2047

outcome.notes: Date and context identified from the prince's French draft reply on f. 4v (answer to a letter of 18 January 1744). Needs the key or more traffic in the same code.
